speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To help me pinpoint the cause, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Progressive Aphasia with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia presenting with acute stroke (Right MCA territory) or rapidly progressive dementia.

I need to clarify if the weakness began suddenly or gradually, and whether he has had any fever, headaches, or neck stiffness in the last week. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast, CBC, ESR, CRP, and Syphilis serology. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial and coronal views.
